chapters.title: Choose a project
chapters.sentence: Choose a project matched to your printer, avoiding tutorials that do not fit your equipment.
chapters.source: VCA pp. 1, 4: VP1; Hauke and Yura on equipment-specific guidance.

chapters.title: Prepare the project
chapters.sentence: Personalize your project and review the setup, bringing scattered printer and material details together.
chapters.source: VCA pp. 4, 6: Yura on combining printer, slicer and filament settings.

chapters.title: Check the printer
chapters.sentence: Check the plate and filament with visual guidance, making each preparation step easier to follow.
chapters.source: VCA pp. 4, 6: Heki on visual steps and exact details; Yura on setup matching.

chapters.title: Inspect the print
chapters.sentence: Inspect the first layer with a visual checklist, reducing guesswork about whether the print looks right.
chapters.source: VCA pp. 6, 8: time lost to late failures; visible checkpoints. Intended benefit, not measured prevention.

chapters.title: Finish the product
chapters.sentence: Follow cooling, removal, and final checks, so you know how to finish after printing ends.
chapters.source: VCA pp. 1, 8–9: task-specific steps and visible checkpoints; applied here to the prototype finishing flow.

chapters.title: Keep what you learned
chapters.sentence: Save your project and notes, keeping what you learned ready for your next attempt.
chapters.source: VCA pp. 4, 7, 9: Kevin on repeated practice; saved progress and later reuse remain hypotheses to test.

method: Isolated browser, real UI actions, capture-only side captions and pointer; held frames edited to 38 seconds. No audio, no simulated print timing.
